entries.title: Acts 14:1
segments: In Iconium it happened that they went together to the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great number both of Jews and of Gentiles believed.

entries.title: Acts 14:2
segments: But the disobedient Jews stirred up the souls of the Gentiles, and embittered them against them against the brothers.

entries.title: Acts 14:3
segments: Long time, therefore, they tarried there, speaking fearlessly in the Lord, who attested the word of his grace by permitting signs and wonders to be performed by their hands.

entries.title: Acts 14:4
segments: But the mass of the city's people was divided; part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

entries.title: Acts 14:5
segments: And when both the Gentiles and the Jews with their ruler made a hostile move to maltreat and to stone them,

entries.title: Acts 14:6
segments: the apostles got wind of it, and made their escape to the Lycaonian towns of Derbe and Lystra and the neighboring country.

entries.title: Acts 14:7
segments: And there they continued to proclaim the gospel.

entries.title: Acts 14:8
segments: Now at Lystra there used to sit a certain man, lame in his feet, a cripple from birth, who had never walked.

entries.title: Acts 14:9
segments: He was listening while Paul was preaching, and Paul, looking intently at him, and perceiving that he had faith to be made whole,

entries.title: Acts 14:10
segments: said in a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet!"

entries.title: Acts 14:11
segments: And he sprang up and began to walk about. Then the crowds, when they saw what Paul had done, shouted in the Lycaonian tongue, saying, "The gods are come down to us in human form."

entries.title: Acts 14:12
segments: And they began to call Barnabas "Zeus," and Paul, since he was the principal speaker, "Hermes";

entries.title: Acts 14:13
segments: and the priest of Zeus, whose temple was at the entrance to the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and along with the crowds was about to offer sacrifices.

entries.title: Acts 14:14
segments: But when the apostles, Paul and Barnabas, heard of it, they rent their garments and rushed out among the crowd, shouting and crying:

entries.title: Acts 14:15
segments: "Men, why are you doing all this? We also are men, with natures like your own! We are bringing you good tidings, that you are to turn from these empty things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that in them is.

entries.title: Acts 14:16
segments: In bygone generations he allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways,

entries.title: Acts 14:17
segments: and yet he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness."

entries.title: Acts 14:18
segments: Even with saying this they with difficulty restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.

entries.title: Acts 14:19
segments: And now a party of Jews came down form Antioch and Iconium, and after persuading the crowds, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing him to be dead.

entries.title: Acts 14:20
segments: But as the disciples collected around him, he rose and went back into the city. The next day he went off with Barnabas into Derbe;

entries.title: Acts 14:21
segments: and after preaching the gospel to that town, and winning many converts, they went back to Lystra and Iconium and Antioch,

entries.title: Acts 14:22
segments: Everywhere they strengthened the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to hold to the faith. "It is through many tribulations," they said, "that we must enter into the kingdom of God."

entries.title: Acts 14:23
segments: They chose elders for them in every church, after prayer and fasting, and commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed.

entries.title: Acts 14:24
segments: Then passing through Pisidia they came to Pamphylia and,

entries.title: Acts 14:25
segments: after preaching the word in Perga, they came down to Attaleia.

entries.title: Acts 14:26
segments: Thence they sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been commended to the grace of God, for the work which they had now completed.

entries.title: Acts 14:27
segments: On their arrival they assembled the church and reported all things that God had done through them, and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.

entries.title: Acts 14:28
segments: And they tarried no little time with the disciples.
